hypothesis: Moving trusted synchronous workflow operations and dashboard task projection work into daemon-owned workers will keep the control API live without changing daemon state ownership or workflow terminal semantics.

metricsCompared.name: control request latency during identical CPU work
metricsCompared.baseline: 699.415 ms with the fixture executed on the daemon main thread
metricsCompared.candidate: 1.007 ms maximum across health, live status, pause, resume, workflow status, and CLI status while the fixture ran in a worker

metricsCompared.name: foreground dashboard large-queue responsiveness
metricsCompared.baseline: The source audit observed synchronous projection rebuilds on every tick and stderr write over roughly 1,600 records
metricsCompared.candidate: One projection refresh, one frame for 250 stderr writes, 2.013 ms live status, and a 500.800 ms end-to-end CLI stop path (authenticated status verification, PID SIGTERM, daemon handler) against a 1,000 ms bound over 1,600 records

metricsCompared.name: worker lifecycle and workflow regression coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: No behavioral control-plane fixture covered success, failure, progress, recovery, and abort across an isolation boundary
metricsCompared.candidate: 215 of 215 affected workflow tests, 6 of 6 worker-boundary/production-commit tests, 3 of 3 live control/terminal/dashboard fixtures, and 10 of 10 architecture/task-policy guards pass; repair attempt 12 additionally passes 52 of 52 critic/probe/semantic-gate/worker-boundary tests, 45 of 45 repair-loop/builder-check/strict-types/layout tests, and 53 of 53 adjacent builder repair/shadow-review workflow tests; repair attempt 14 passes 61 of 61 focused merge-gate, conflict-resolution, builder, blocked-promoter, source-policy, and real-worker tests followed by 367 of 367 broad Git/builder/blocked-promoter/control-terminal/dashboard tests; repair attempt 15 passes 15 of 15 focused digest/finalizer/worker tests, 72 of 72 expanded live-control/runtime tests, and 398 of 398 critical workflow/daemon/strict-types tests, including a 1,200 ms terminal finalizer that keeps health, status, pause, and resume within the 500 ms bound; repair attempt 17 passes 49 of 49 focused workflow/source-boundary/real-worker tests, 15 of 15 adjacent blocking-operation/calibration tests, and 16 of 16 strict-type/source-size policy tests; repair attempt 20 passes the full 370-test eval-harness suite plus 42 focused core runtime, strict-types, and layout tests, including cadence worker delegation and real child-process abort; recovery is a canonical failed run followed by a control-API retry with persisted retryOf metadata

rationale: The candidate preserves the daemon as the sole owner of live workflow state while isolating definition-owned, structured-clone operations, including daily-digest history/task aggregation, builder terminal Git/worktree reconciliation and claim/port-lease finalization, builder merge-gate Git and validation phases, merged-worktree cleanup, blocked-task promotion and owner-outcome mutation, progress-review full-queue dedupe and staged task mutation, evaluator-calibration Git-history proposal and task mutation, weekly eval-harness fixture discovery/materialization/subprocess execution/baseline persistence, builder evidence projection and mobile staged-Git inspection, builder task-state and success-criteria repair inspection/staging, improver and builder staged-diff/repository checks, critic task/diff/product-evidence/runtime-probe inspection, improver semantic-gate diff and commit-message inspection, inbox/research shadow-review Git diff assembly, security-review Git baselines and recursive candidate scans, scope-improver full-queue inspection and staged task mutation, and builder recovery reconciliation, while using asynchronous APIs for package commands and lightweight Git status reads. Code steps and terminal finalizers share the same daemon-owned blocking runner, and the merge-conflict agent remains daemon-coordinated between worker phases. The tied baseline/candidate fixture remains well inside the 500 ms request bound; a deliberately blocking terminal finalizer keeps health, status, pause, and resume inside that bound; the authenticated CLI stop path completes inside its 1,000 ms end-to-end bound; dashboard refreshes are cached and non-overlapping; terminal metadata and progress/error/abort semantics are covered; the cadence worker forwards heartbeats and terminates its active fixture subprocess on abort; recovery uses a canonical failed run and persisted control-API retry metadata; and type, build, architecture, and focused workflow checks pass.
